text:
sylvie: quick question about rate limit headers for streaming endpoints — do we send final X-RateLimit-* on the last chunk, or include them in the initial response and then again?

mohit: For streaming we currently emit headers on the initial 200 and chunk frames don't carry HTTP headers. We discussed adding control frames but haven't implemented. We can't modify HTTP headers after body start.

dana: That matches infra constraints. Important: clients expecting `X-RateLimit-Remaining` after a stream finishes will be left hanging. Suggest adding a final control event in the stream payload like `{"_rd_rl":{"remaining":123,"reset":1723457999}}` so clients get the same info.

kevin: That seems reasonable. Concern: some clients parse stream as plain text. We should namespace control events to reduce breakage — `__rd_rl` or `redwood_rate_limit_event`.

sylvie: Good point. Also for non-stream endpoints: should we standardize on `Retry-After` (seconds) + `X-RateLimit-Reset` (epoch seconds) + `X-RateLimit-Limit`/`Remaining`? Current headers exist but semantics for per-route vs global are unclear.

mohit: Proposal (PR #456):
- `X-RateLimit-Limit`: numeric limit for the scope (route/account/global)
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: tokens left for that scope
- `X-RateLimit-Scope`: one of `route|account|global`
- `X-RateLimit-Reset`: epoch seconds when this window resets
- on 429 responses include `Retry-After` with seconds until safe retry
Keep headers small and consistent.

dana: Will we expose burst capacity info? e.g., separate header `X-RateLimit-Burst-Window` or `X-RateLimit-Burst-Capacity`? Clients might use that to smooth retries.

kevin: I'd prefer minimal additions. If needed, `X-RateLimit-Burst-Capacity` as an optional integer when bursts are allowed. If header absent assume no extra burst. Too many headers confuse clients.

sylvie: Backcompat: consumers expect a 429 body like `{"error":"rate_limited"}`. Can we add a `metadata` object in the JSON body with the same info as headers so clients that can't read headers still get guidance?

mohit: Yes — include `metadata` on 429 responses: e.g. `{"error":"rate_limited", "metadata":{"scope":"route","limit":1000,"remaining":0,"reset":1723457999}}`. Keep the top-level error exactly the same to avoid breaking checks.

dana: Edge-case we need to call out in docs: long-running requests that consume tokens during processing. Do we ever return 429 after we already charged tokens? That would be bad — clients pay but get an error. We should do admission checks and reserve tokens at start, refund on failure.

kevin: Agreed — admission + optimistic reserve. If job is accepted we shouldn't return 429 later unless there's a bug. Refund logic for failures must be explicit. We'll document refund semantics.

rate-limiter-bot: deploy scheduled: Mon 03/18 02:00 UTC — canary 50% will start emitting new headers and stream control events. Rollback window 30m.

sylvie: Action items: @mohit update PR to include stream-control event example and header matrix, @dana update docs for admission/refund semantics, @kevin verify rollback plan and telemetry. I'll add TODOs to the API contract doc and tag the owners.

mohit: ack. I'll include a curl + stream example in the PR: 
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# 200 OK
# X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
# X-RateLimit-Remaining: 74
# X-RateLimit-Scope: route
# X-RateLimit-Reset: 1723457999
# ...stream chunks...
# {"text":"..."}
# {"_rd_rl":{"remaining":73,"reset":1723457999}}
```

dana: thanks — small nit: use `"_rd_rl"` (with two underscores) for the control event namespace so it's unlikely to collide.

kevin: lgtm :thumbsup:
